<reason>Side A wins the instrument clash: its hold-or-waive credibility dilemma, bulk-cargo cost distinction, and two-tier fleet risks survive, while B relies on hypothetical revenue recycling and repeats that container costs are trivial. A also shows a binding intensity trajectory can force cuts now and compel zero-carbon fuels when deliverable, neutralizing B's claim that only a fuel timetable ends fossil shipping.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Most decisive was A's Rebuttal 2: it distinguished imperfect verification workable for pricing from a binary fuel mandate that rewards certificate fraud, and recast its intensity standard as a dated binding trajectory rather than an undefined endpoint.</best_rebuttal>
